name: Giving (dāna)
method_summary: Give because it ought to be given, to one who makes no return, at the right place and time, to a worthy recipient (sāttvic, 17.20); giving is not to be abandoned but done without attachment and fruit (18.5–6).

warnings.text: Giving for a return, for fruit or grudgingly is rājasic.

name: The Gītā's meditation (dhyāna-yoga, BhG 6.10–32)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 18.51–53: yoked with a purified understanding, restraining oneself with steadiness, relinquishing sound and the other objects, casting off passion and aversion, resorting to solitude, eating lightly, controlling speech, body and mind, ever intent on the yoga of meditation, taking refuge in dispassion, letting go of ahaṅkāra, force, arrogance, desire, anger and possessions, without 'mine' and at peace.
prerequisites: The perfection (siddhi) of 18.49–50, from which the course to Brahman is described.

method_summary: Do sacrifice, giving, austerity and allotted action because they ought to be done, giving up attachment and fruit (18.6, 18.9); since the embodied cannot give up action entirely, relinquishing the fruit of action makes one a relinquisher (18.2, 18.11).

name: Performing rites with 'oṃ tat sat'
method_summary: Summary as the text states it: the acts of sacrifice, giving and austerity of the expounders of Brahman begin with the utterance of 'oṃ' (17.24); with 'tat', those seeking release perform sacrifice, austerity and giving without aiming at fruit (17.25); 'sat' is applied to what is real and good, to praiseworthy acts, to steadfastness in sacrifice, austerity and giving, and to action for that purpose (17.26–27). The three words are the threefold designation of Brahman (17.23).

warnings.text: Whatever is offered, given, practised or done without faith is 'asat', of no account here or hereafter.

notes: This edition's 17.23 omits 'oṃ' (see the teaching's notes).

name: Sāttvic food
method_summary: The text classifies foods by the type of person to whom they are dear: foods increasing life, sattva, strength, health, happiness and delight, savoury, smooth, substantial and agreeable, are dear to the sāttvic (17.8); pungent, sour, salty, very hot, sharp, dry and burning foods, which bring pain, grief and disease, to the rājasic (17.9); stale, tasteless, putrid, overnight, leftover and impure food to the tāmasic (17.10). It states effects but gives no explicit rule of diet.

warnings.text: Rājasic foods bring pain, grief and disease.
Spoiled, tasteless, putrid, stale, leftover and impure food is dear to the tāmasic.

name: Austerity of body, speech and mind

names.name: Austerity of body, speech and mind

method_summary: Bodily: worship of gods, the twice-born, teachers and the wise; purity, straightforwardness, celibacy, non-harming (17.14). Verbal: speech that does not agitate, true, pleasant and beneficial, and the practice of recitation (17.15). Mental: clarity of mind, gentleness, silence, self-restraint, purity of disposition (17.16). It is sāttvic when practised with supreme faith by the disciplined who do not desire its fruit (17.17).

warnings.text: Austerity done for respect, honour and reverence, or with hypocrisy, is rājasic, unstable and impermanent.
Austerity done from a deluded notion, with torment of oneself or to ruin another, is tāmasic.
Terrible austerity not enjoined by scripture, done with hypocrisy and the sense of 'I', tormenting the body's elements and the Lord within, marks those of demonic resolve.

names.name: Sacrifice and eating its remains (yajña, yajña-śiṣṭa)

method_summary: Summary as chs. 17–18 state it (no procedure is given): sacrifice offered according to injunction by those not desiring its fruit, the mind set on 'it simply ought to be offered', is sāttvic (17.11); the rites of the expounders of Brahman begin with 'oṃ' (17.24); sacrifice, giving and austerity purify the wise, are not to be abandoned, and are to be done giving up attachment and fruit (18.5–6).

warnings.text: Sacrifice for fruit or display is rājasic.
Sacrifice without injunction, distributed food, mantras, fee or faith is tāmasic.
Sacrifices in name only, with hypocrisy and not by injunction, are the demonic's.
